name: Eritrea

facts.religion: Christian about half (Orthodox, Catholic, Protestant), Sunni Muslim about half

snapshot: One of the world's most closed states, ruled since independence in 1993 by Isaias Afwerki with no elections, no constitution in force and indefinite military service.
culture: Eritrea's nine ethnic groups include Tigrinya-speaking highlanders and Tigre, Afar and other lowland peoples, with roughly equal Christian and Muslim populations. Asmara, built largely under Italian rule in the 1930s, is a UNESCO-listed showcase of modernist architecture, with Art Deco cinemas and cafés where espresso culture survives. Cycling is hugely popular, and Eritrean riders have competed in the Tour de France.
society: National service, meant to last 18 months, is in practice open-ended, and it drives a steady exodus of young people across deserts and the Mediterranean. There is no independent press. Mining, mainly gold and copper, is the main export earner. Families depend on remittances, and the diaspora is taxed by the state.
baseline: Isaias Afwerki has ruled since independence from Ethiopia after a 30-year war. Eritrean troops fought alongside Ethiopia's army in Tigray in 2020 to 2022, but relations with Addis Ababa have since soured, with Ethiopia's prime minister talking about access to the Red Sea, raising fears of a new war. The ruling PFDJ is the only legal party.
